note: LIVE DATA — this file and goinggone-lots-catalogue.json are the source for the lots in goinggone.html. Real purchasable items with verified prices; every entry has a source URL and the date its price was read. Nothing here is invented — if a price could not be verified, the item is not in this file. AFTER EDITING, run `node scripts/build-goinggone-lots.js` to re-embed, or unit/goinggone.test.js will fail. This half is hand-researched, one search per item, with fuller confidence notes. RULE: a lot's name and desc must NEVER state or hint at the price — the whole game is guessing it. No dollar amounts, no spelled-out prices, no 'four grand', and no comparisons either ('costs more than a car', 'the cheapest lot here'); unit/goinggone.test.js fails on any of them.
sourcingNote: Amazon was the original intent and is not usable: WebFetch on an Amazon product page returns HTTP 500 (Amazon blocks automated fetches) and site-restricted search returns category pages with no prices. The constraint was dropped in favour of any verifiable retailer. Re-test Amazon before assuming it is still blocked.

band.note: $1–$10,000 is the band the ORDINARY lots are spread across, not a hard cap. Items genuinely worth more are allowed and keep their full value — the bargain stands. See goinggoneplan-realitems.md for why, and why capping is the wrong lever.

lots.name: Used 20ft Shipping Container, Delivered

lots.confidenceNote: Consistent across independent dealers: $1,800–$3,800 delivered depending on grade and distance from a depot. $2,800 sits mid-range. A good lot because everyone thinks they know this one and almost nobody does — and the delivery is a third of it.

lots.confidenceNote: New combo machines cluster at $3,000–$5,500, with the wider snack/drink/combo market $3,000–$10,000 depending on refrigeration and card payment. $4,200 sits mid-range. Strong lot: everyone has used one, nobody has priced one.

lots.name: Orange Traffic Cone (28in, reflective)

lots.confidenceNote: Read directly off the retail page: $14.50 at qty 1-14, marked down from $18.40. Fills the empty $1-100 band. Good lot because official-looking road furniture reads as expensive and isn't.

lots.name: One Regulation Bowling Pin

lots.name: Supermarket Shopping Trolley

Judgement call for the game: it is a real, guessable, surprisingly-priced object, but check the room — it may not be the lot you want between the candy floss machine and the alpaca.

lots.name: Home Battery System, 10kWh Installed
lots.desc: The wall-mounted battery that runs the house when the power cuts.

lots.name: 6ft Privacy Fence Panel, Installed

Re-check against a materials-only listing before shipping — the installed/materials distinction is exactly the kind of thing that makes a lot feel wrong.

researchLog.learned: Item-specific searches work; category searches do not. 'Surprisingly expensive everyday objects' returned inflation journalism with no purchasable items. Every good lot so far came from naming the THING and asking its price. Budget roughly one search per item and corroborate across dealers where a single retail listing does not exist.

Top-tier pass, driven by a test failure rather than a hunch: the band-depth check reported the $50,000+ tier holding only 8 lots, all of them commercial catering equipment from the bulk harvest — so the last round of a three-round game was choosing between a pot-and-pan washer and a pizza oven. Fourteen hand-researched lots added, nine of them over $50,000. What worked: naming an ICONIC OBJECT and asking its price ('Zamboni', 'Routemaster', 'gyrocopter') rather than asking for expensive things. Dealer inventory pages (Firetrucks Unlimited, AutoGyro USA) and marketplace medians (AeroGurus, 51 Cessna 152 listings) give the firmest numbers; manufacturers of one-off equipment mostly refuse to publish and need a dealer or a pricing guide instead. Machinio blocks fetching (403). NOTE THE ARITHMETIC CEILING: a lot is only ever dealt when its reserve fits the richest bankroll (value <= 1.8 x ceiling at RESERVE_FRAC 0.25 / REACH 0.45), so with round-3 bankrolls near $25,000-$60,000 the useful sweet spot is $50,000-$110,000. A private aircraft DOES fit there — a used Cessna 152 is $67,000 — but a business jet never will without a much larger economy.

pricingNote2026: MEMORY PRICES ARE MOVING IN 2026 and several computing lots have already re-priced: Mac mini $599 -> $799 (June 2026), Mac Studio M3 Ultra +$1,300 with the 256GB/512GB options withdrawn entirely (March-May 2026), DGX Spark +18% on LPDDR5X shortages. Re-check every computing lot before a session; these are the fastest-rotting prices in the file, and the reason capturedOn is shown on the bidding card.
bandGap: The $5,000-$10,000 band is the thin one: 13 lots across both files, against the 10 that a full 10-player table draws. Top it toward ~25 before heavy use. Every other band has 28-42.
